`src/sort.rs` implements **quicksort** with the **Lomuto partition scheme**. The pivot is always the last element, `arr[len - 1]`. It recurses on the two halves around the pivot.

**Worst case: O(n²) time.**
- This happens when the last-element pivot lands at an extreme every time. Already-sorted, reverse-sorted, and all-equal input all do this. Each partition then splits n into 0 and n−1.
- Equal elements trigger it because the partition test is `<=`, so every equal element goes to the left side.
- The recursion depth in that case is O(n), so stack space is also O(n) worst case. A large sorted input could overflow the stack.

Average and best case are O(n log n). The doc comment in the file says the same.

I only read the file. I didn't run or change anything.
